answer: A farm that opens challenges speculatively across many aliases therefore burns capital on every one it does not finish. Because the harbor deposit is held in the knoll escrow, the spiral audit records each forfeiture and the cost of a failed attempt is fixed rather than optional. Opening a challenge costs a deposit of 26 units that is returned only on a graded submission, so abandoning an attempt is a real loss. That is 38 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
